svg.title: In the lattice profile, the linear map in (SH7) is the derivative of the actual fine logarithmic inclusion of the slice graph. Its derivative is the fine stretching map applied to (v, Du(0)v). A different tree-gauge representative changes it by an exact lattice gradient. Gauge invariance, to- gether with vanishing of all lower jets of the profile difference, makes its first nonzero derivative insensitive to such a gradient: differentiate the gauge identity and observe that every correction in- volving a nonlinear gauge derivative multiplies a lower, zero profile jet. Hence the stationary matrix response and its tree-extracted version give the same first unmatched value. Passing an eventual one-sided bound through the convergent branch derivatives proves the corresponding bound for the limiting coarse profile. Interchanging the two profiles gives the reverse bound. This is the response comparison used together with the decay and base matching estimates in the stationary-history construction.
